summary: Frozen baseline and current branch were measured with the same Release OrdinaryDispatchGitTests fixtures. Baseline 9dc95184896118c96f34493da28ce40bf5b3d8d6: cold ReadFile, GetAgentInstructions and GetProjectDetails each used 104 Git process starts / 6 remote fetches (561–646 ms); warm Working calls used 0/0. The baseline run passed the three cost fixtures and failed only the newly added fence negative control (12 Git process starts instead of 0). Assigned branch 83c688bae3f86ad85dd91a76303408b39a98300d: all four fixtures pass; each cold path uses 75 process starts / 3 remote fetches (330–429 ms), and warm paths remain 0/0. This is 28% fewer Git processes, 50% fewer fetches, and roughly 33% lower measured cold latency. Fresh origin/main is 142f2bd4b2728ea61e18a9d51f7c663c7951e182; its delta from the pinned base is confined to LedgerStore initial source-checkout verification and ReviewWorkflow source binding, with no Client/SignalR dispatch or inbox change to backport.
nextAction: Implement the remaining request-local read optimization: when a fresh snapshot has just been verified for automatic-activation eligibility but the task is ActivationIneligible (or a read-only activation conflict is reconciled), preserve that same snapshot for post-dispatch Working guidance instead of invalidating it and fetching again. Add a focused Ready-but-Closed-task regression that compares payload/instructions/state and asserts one fewer remote fetch, then run the focused Release tests and request independent review.
